## 1. Verdict: are data checksums enabled on a fresh PostgreSQL 18 cluster?

**Yes — enabled.** In PostgreSQL 18, `initdb` enables data checksums by default, so a cluster created with no checksum-related flag has checksums ON.

Grounds:
- `initdb` reference, `-k` / `--data-checksums`: "Use checksums on data pages to help detect corruption by the I/O system that would otherwise be silent. **This is enabled by default; use `--no-data-checksums` to disable checksums.**" (postgresql.org/docs/18/app-initdb.html)
- PostgreSQL 18 release notes, Migration to Version 18, incompatibilities: "**Change initdb default to enable data checksums** (Greg Sabino Mullane) — Checksums can be disabled with the new initdb option `--no-data-checksums`. pg_upgrade requires matching cluster checksum settings, so this new option can be useful to upgrade non-checksum old clusters."
- Monitoring chapter, 28.2: "**By default, data pages are protected by checksums**, but this can optionally be disabled for a cluster."

This is the behavior change versus PostgreSQL 17 and earlier, where checksums were off unless `initdb -k` was given. Do not carry the pre-18 default forward into a PG18 runbook.

Scope of the setting (matters for both ask 2 and ask 3): "Data checksums are enabled or disabled at the **full cluster level**, and cannot be specified individually for databases or tables." There is no per-database, per-table or per-tablespace checksum setting, so "matching" in ask 3 is a single cluster-wide boolean comparison.

## 2. How are they switched off?

Two supported paths. Pick by whether the cluster already exists.

### 2a. At creation time (the normal path, and the only one that avoids rewriting every page)

```bash
initdb -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data --no-data-checksums
```

`--no-data-checksums` is **new in PostgreSQL 18** — it exists precisely because the default flipped. It is the negative form of `-k/--data-checksums`; it takes no argument. Combine it with the rest of your usual flags, e.g.:

```bash
initdb -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data \
       --no-data-checksums \
       --encoding=UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8
```

### 2b. On an existing cluster (offline rewrite)

`data_checksums` is a **read-only** configuration variable, so it cannot be changed with `ALTER SYSTEM` / `postgresql.conf`; a restart will not flip it. The only post-creation method is the offline tool `pg_checksums`:

```bash
# 1. Clean shutdown of the cluster — pg_checksums requires it offline.
pg_ctl -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data stop -m fast

# 2. Confirm it is really down (no postmaster.pid holder).
pg_ctl -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data status

# 3. Disable checksums: rewrites every data page in the cluster.
pg_checksums --disable -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data

# 4. Restart.
pg_ctl -D /var/lib/pgsql/18/data start
```

Operational notes for 2b (DBA practice, not doc quotations): the cluster must have been shut down cleanly (not crash-recovered) before `pg_checksums` will run; the operation touches every relation in every database and therefore takes time proportional to cluster size, and it must be repeated on each node of a replication set or the standbys will diverge from the primary's page format. Schedule it in a maintenance window, and take a base backup first.

### 2c. Verify the resulting state — always, don't trust the default

```sql
SHOW data_checksums;      -- 'on' = checksums enabled, 'off' = disabled
```

or, with the server down:

```bash
pg_controldata /var/lib/pgsql/18/data | grep -i 'checksum'
# Data page checksum version: 1   -> enabled
# Data page checksum version: 0   -> disabled
```

`data_checksums` is read-only and cluster-wide; `pg_controldata` reads the same fact from `pg_control`. Either is authoritative — do not infer the state from the initdb command line you think was used.

## 3. What must hold for checksum settings when running pg_upgrade?

**The old cluster and the new cluster must have matching checksum settings.** This is a requirement, not a recommendation:

> "**pg_upgrade requires matching cluster checksum settings**, so this new option can be useful to upgrade non-checksum old clusters." — PostgreSQL 18 release notes, E.7.2 Migration to Version 18.

Because checksums are a whole-cluster property with no per-database/table/tablespace granularity, "matching" means exactly one comparison: old cluster's `data_checksums` == new cluster's `data_checksums`. pg_upgrade compares cluster-level control-file settings ("pg_upgrade will check `pg_controldata` to make sure all settings are compatible before starting the upgrade"), so a mismatch is caught up front rather than discovered mid-upgrade.

Upgrade matrix:

| Old cluster (checksums) | New PG18 cluster created with | Result |
|---|---|---|
| off (typical ≤17 default) | plain `initdb` → **on** | **Mismatch — upgrade will not pass its checks.** Re-run initdb with `--no-data-checksums`. |
| off | `initdb --no-data-checksums` → off | OK — this is the case the new option was added for. |
| on (`initdb -k` in ≤17) | plain `initdb` → on | OK — the PG18 default now matches. |
| on | `initdb --no-data-checksums` → off | Mismatch. Either drop the flag or disable on the old cluster first. |

Two ways to resolve an off→on mismatch, both valid:
1. **Match down (usual, cheapest):** `initdb --no-data-checksums` for the new cluster. Nothing on the old cluster is touched. This is the documented use case.
2. **Match up:** enable checksums on the *old* cluster before upgrading, offline (`pg_checksums --enable -D <old_datadir>` with the old cluster stopped), then let the new PG18 cluster keep the default (on). This costs a full page rewrite of the old cluster and buys you checksums going forward.

Timing rule: settle the checksum decision **before** the upgrade run, at `initdb` time on the new cluster. Do not attempt to toggle checksums on the new cluster after pg_upgrade has linked/cloned/swapped files, and do not plan to "fix it after the upgrade" — the settings must match at the moment pg_upgrade runs.

Caveat on sourcing: the PG18 `pg_upgrade` reference page itself contains **no occurrence of the words "checksums", "data checksums", "enabled", "disabled" or "off"** (full-text search of the fetched page, 34,905 characters, sha256 4b96b8964844; the same holds for the /current/ copy, 34,869 characters, sha256 83c72cd628b1). The matching requirement is stated in the release notes (quoted above) and implied by the generic "compatible initdb flags that match the old cluster" / `pg_controldata` compatibility check in the pg_upgrade procedure. So the constraint is documented, just not on the pg_upgrade man page.

## 4. Condensed runbook

```bash
# New PG18 cluster, checksums off (e.g. to match a pre-18 old cluster):
initdb -D $PGDATA --no-data-checksums

# Or, later, on an existing PG18 cluster, offline:
pg_ctl -D $PGDATA stop -m fast
pg_checksums --disable -D $PGDATA
pg_ctl -D $PGDATA start

# Verify either way:
psql -c 'SHOW data_checksums;'        # on | off
pg_controldata $PGDATA | grep -i checksum   # version 1 | 0

# Before pg_upgrade: old and new must agree; check both clusters with pg_controldata.
```
cautions: Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 18 on postgresql.org/docs/18/pgupgrade.html and 19 on postgresql.org/docs/current/pgupgrade.html. The first reads: "pg_ctl -D /opt/PostgreSQL/12 stop pg_ctl -D /opt/PostgreSQL/18 stop or on Windows, using the proper service names:"

# Compliance note — Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (machinery): application date, repeal of Directive 2006/42/EC, and in-force status on 17 November 2026

## 1. Answers

| # | Ask | Answer |
|---|-----|--------|
| 1 | Constraint: read against the Regulation **as corrected** and in force on **17 November 2026** | Applied — see §2 (version determination). The corrected/consolidated text is used throughout; the uncorrected OJ text is used only as a control. |
| 2 | From which date does the Regulation apply and the Directive stop applying? | **20 January 2027** — one and the same date for both events. |
| 3 | Is Directive 2006/42/EC still in force today (17 November 2026)? | **Yes.** The repeal takes effect on 20 January 2027, i.e. 64 days after the reference date. Until then the Directive is the operative product-safety regime for machinery. |

Legal basis, corrected text:

- **Article 54, second subparagraph:** "It shall apply from ►C1 **20 January 2027** ◄." (with earlier partial application of listed Articles, §5 below).
- **Article 51(2):** "Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from ►C1 **20 January 2027** ◄."

Because the Regulation's date of application and the effective date of the Directive's repeal coincide, there is no regulatory gap and no overlap: on 20 January 2027 the Directive ceases to apply and the Regulation becomes fully applicable on the same day.

## 2. Which text governs (ask 1)

EUR-Lex records for Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (OJ L 165, 29.6.2023, p. 1):

- **Amended by:** ►M1 Regulation (EU) 2024/2748 (9 October 2024, OJ L 2748, 8.11.2024); ►M2 Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (8 July 2026, OJ L 1744, 24.7.2026).
- **Corrected by:** ►C1 Corrigendum, OJ L 169, 4.7.2023, p. 35 ((EU) 2023/1230).
- **Consolidated versions listed:** 29/06/2023 (initial), 29/05/2026 (001.001), **27/07/2026 (002.001) — current version**; status shown as "In force".

For a reference date of 17 November 2026 the current consolidated version is **02023R1230 — EN — 27.07.2026 — 002.001**, which incorporates M1, M2 and the C1 correction. EUR-Lex marks consolidated texts as "purely a documentation tool … no legal effect"; the authentic text is the OJ publication as corrected by OJ L 169, 4.7.2023, p. 35. The consolidated texts reproduce the correction inline with ►C1 markers, so the corrected wording is what is read below. The 29/05/2026 consolidated version (001.001, i.e. M1 but not yet M2) and the Commission's LEGISSUM summary 4682019 give the same operative dates, so the answer does not depend on M2.

## 3. Corrigendum effect — why the answer is 20 January 2027 and not 14 January 2027

The initial OJ text (unconsolidated, CELEX:32023R1230) carries a set of dates that the corrigendum replaced. Side-by-side, every date moved by **+6 days**:

| Provision | Initial OJ text | Corrected text (►C1) |
|---|---|---|
| Art 54, 2nd subpara. — Regulation applies from | 14 January 2027 | **20 January 2027** |
| Art 51(2) — Directive 2006/42/EC repealed with effect from | 14 January 2027 | **20 January 2027** |
| Art 52(1) — Chapter VI applies to pre-cut-off products from | 13 July 2023 | **19 July 2023** |
| Art 52(1) — cut-off for products placed on the market under the Directive | 14 January 2027 | **20 January 2027** |
| Art 54(a) — Articles 26–42 | 14 January 2024 | **20 January 2024** |
| Art 54(b) — Article 50(1) | 14 October 2023 | **20 October 2023** |
| Art 54(c) — Article 6(7), Articles 48 and 52 | 13 July 2023 | **19 July 2023** |
| Art 54(d) — Article 6(2)–(6), (8), (11), Articles 47 and 53(3) | 14 July 2024 | **20 July 2024** |
| Art 50(2) — notification of national penalty rules "by" | 14 October 2026 | **20 October 2026** |

Coherence test that confirms the corrigendum governs: the Regulation entered into force on "the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal" (Art 54, first subparagraph; OJ publication 29 June 2023) = **19 July 2023**. The corrected Article 52(1)/54(c) date is exactly 19 July 2023. The uncorrected 13 July 2023 would have made an obligation applicable six days *before* entry into force, which is legally impossible — a positive indication that the C1 correction, not the initial text, states the operative dates.

## 4. Amendment sweep (has anything changed the dates since publication?)

- **M1 — Regulation (EU) 2024/2748** (applies from 29 May 2026 per LEGISSUM 4682019): the consolidated version of **29/05/2026 (001.001)**, which incorporates M1, still reads "It shall apply from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄" and "Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄". No change.
- **M2 — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744** (OJ L 1744, 24.7.2026): the consolidated version of **27/07/2026 (002.001)**, which incorporates M1 + M2, still reads the same two dates, and Article 54 still reads "It shall apply from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄" with subparagraphs (a)–(d) at the corrected dates. No change.
- **No further corrigendum** appears in the consolidated-text header beyond C1, and no act in force by the reference date alters Articles 51, 52 or 54 in respect of these dates.

Conclusion: as at 17 November 2026 the corrected, amended, in-force text fixes **20 January 2027** for both the full application of the Regulation and the effective repeal of Directive 2006/42/EC.

## 5. Article 54 in full (corrected), for the record

> "**Article 54 — Entry into force and application**
> This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
> It shall apply from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄.
> However, the following Articles shall apply from the following dates:
> (a) Articles 26 to 42 from ►C1 20 January 2024 ◄;
> (b) Article 50(1) from ►C1 20 October 2026 ◄;
> (c) Article 6(7) and Articles 48 and 52 from ►C1 19 July 2023 ◄;
> (d) Article 6(2) to (6), (8) and (11) and Articles 47 and 53(3) from ►C1 20 July 2024 ◄.
> This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States."

*Source discrepancy to be aware of, immaterial to the asks:* the consolidated PDF (02023R1230-20260727) prints Article 54(b) as "20 October **2026**", whereas LEGISSUM 4682019 prints "Article 50(1) from 20 October **2023**". The 2023 reading is the one consistent with the corrigendum pattern (+6 days from 14 October 2023) and with the fact that Article 50(1) governs the penalties framework that Member States had to be able to apply well before 2027. Neither reading touches the answer to ask 2 or ask 3. Verify against the authentic OJ text before relying on Article 50(1) for any other purpose.

## 6. Article 51 and Article 52 (corrected), as quoted

> "**Article 51 — Repeals**
> 1. Directive 73/361/EEC is repealed. …
> 2. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄. References to the repealed Directive 2006/42/EC shall be construed as references to this Regulation and shall be read in accordance with the correlation table in Annex XII."

> "**Article 52 — Transitional provisions**
> 1. Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products which were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄. However, Chapter VI of this Regulation shall apply, from ►C1 19 July 2023 ◄, mutatis mutandis to such products instead of Article 11 of that Directive, including products for which a procedure has already been initiated under Article 11 of Directive 2006/42/EC.
> 2. EC type-examination certificates and approval decisions issued in accordance with Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC shall remain valid until they expire."

Recital (from the same text): "It is necessary to provide for sufficient time for economic operators to comply with their obligations under this Regulation, and for Member States to set up the administrative infrastructure necessary for its application. The application of this Regulation should therefore be deferred …" — the rationale for the deferred application date; it does not alter it.

## 7. Derivation of the verdict on ask 3 (in force vs. applies vs. repealed)

Three distinct concepts must not be conflated:

1. **Entry into force** — 19 July 2023 (Art 54, first subparagraph). The Regulation has been *in force* since then.
2. **Application** — in full from **20 January 2027** (Art 54, second subparagraph), with the staggered earlier applications in §5.
3. **Repeal of the Directive** — "with effect from" **20 January 2027** (Art 51(2)). A repeal expressed to take effect on a future date leaves the repealed act in force until that date.

On the reference date, 17 November 2026:

- 20 January 2027 has not yet arrived; therefore Article 51(2) has not yet produced its effect and **Directive 2006/42/EC remains in force and remains the applicable conformity-assessment regime** for machinery placed on the market on that date.
- The Regulation is in force but, save for the Articles listed in Article 54(a)–(d), not yet applicable.
- The transitional provisions do **not** extend the Directive's life: Article 52(1) preserves the *free movement* of products already placed on the market under the Directive before 20 January 2027 (a product-level grandfathering rule), and Article 52(2) preserves the validity of EC type-examination certificates until they expire (a certificate-level rule). Neither keeps the Directive itself in force after 20 January 2027. In particular, Article 52(1) second sentence already displaces Article 11 of the Directive with Chapter VI of the Regulation as from 19 July 2023, which shows the Directive's regime is being wound down, not prolonged.

Verdict: **yes, the Directive is still in force on 17 November 2026**, with 64 days remaining before its repeal takes effect (13 days remaining in November + 31 in December + 20 in January = 64).

## 8. Handling of the harness proof of absence for ask 2 (explicit record)

A proof of absence was supplied for ask 2 against **https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1230** (674,353 characters, fetched 2026-11-24T02:01:23Z, sha256 95e9a46bca4d): none of "20 January 2027", "from 20 January 2027", "shall apply from 20 January 2027", "shall cease to apply from 20 January 2027", "Directive 2006/42/EC shall cease to apply", "Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 shall apply" appears in that page.

That finding is **correct and expected, and it does not create a gap in the grounding**, for the following reason: the page named is the **initial, unconsolidated OJ act** (CELEX:32023R1230). It carries the *pre-corrigendum* dates — "It shall apply from 14 January 2027", "Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027", "Member States shall, by 14 October 2026", "from 13 July 2023". The corrigendum (►C1, OJ L 169, 4.7.2023, p. 35) is precisely what replaced those strings with the 20 January 2027 family of dates. The absence of "20 January 2027" from the uncorrected page therefore *corroborates* the corrigendum analysis in §3 rather than showing that the date is unstated anywhere.

The request fixes the object of analysis as the text **as corrected** and in force on 17 November 2026, and that text is present in the grounding and states the date expressly:

- 02023R1230 — EN — **29.05.2026** — 001.001: "It shall apply from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄"; "Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄".
- 02023R1230 — EN — **27.07.2026** — 002.001 (PDF, CELEX:02023R1230-20260727): "It shall apply from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄"; "Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from ►C1 20 January 2027 ◄".
- LEGISSUM 4682019: "Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 will apply from 20 January 2027"; "repeals and replaces Directive 2006/42/EC as of 20 January 2027".

Accordingly ask 2 is **not** recorded as not-stated and **not** recorded as blocked: the answer to it is not "the page states none" — the corrected pages state it. A figure is therefore given: 20 January 2027.

## 9. Internal consistency checks performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Regulation application date = Directive repeal effective date | Yes — both 20 January 2027 (Art 54 vs Art 51(2)); no gap, no overlap. |
| Stated repeal date later than the reference date (else the verdict would be wrong) | 20 Jan 2027 > 17 Nov 2026 → Directive still in force. Consistent. |
| Days remaining computed from the two stated dates | 64 (13 + 31 + 20). Consistent with both dates. |
| Entry-into-force arithmetic (29.6.2023 + 20 days) | 19 July 2023, matching corrected Art 52(1)/54(c). Consistent. |
| Corrigendum shift uniform across all affected dates | +6 days in every case (§3). Consistent. |
| Consolidated version used is the latest listed as current at the reference date | 27/07/2026 (002.001); the 29/05/2026 version gives the same dates, so M2 is not load-bearing. |

## 10. Practical consequences as at 17 November 2026 (for operational use)

- Machinery placed on the market **on or after 20 January 2027** must be compliant with Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (CE marking, EU declaration of conformity, technical documentation retained at least 10 years — Arts 10–11 and Annexes).
- Machinery **placed on the market before 20 January 2027** in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC may continue to be made available (Art 52(1)); national authorities may not impede that.
- Chapter VI of the Regulation (market surveillance / Union safeguard procedure) already applies to such legacy products, in place of Article 11 of the Directive, from 19 July 2023.
- EC type-examination certificates and approval decisions issued under Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC remain valid until expiry (Art 52(2)) — no re-certification is triggered by the repeal as such, though certificates cannot be renewed under the Directive after 20 January 2027.
- Member States' penalty notifications under Article 50(2) fell due on 20 October 2026 (corrected date) — already past at the reference date.
- Any declaration of conformity, technical file or contractual statement asserting "Directive 2006/42/EC applies" remains correct until 19 January 2027 inclusive and must switch to the Regulation from 20 January 2027.

## 11. Re-verification triggers (what would change this answer)

The answer rests on Articles 51(2) and 54 of the corrected text. It would be displaced only by an act adopted before 20 January 2027 that amends those provisions or defers the application date (for example a further corrigendum, or a postponement adopted under a simplification/omnibus instrument). No such act appears in the consolidated-text header as at the reference date: the header lists M1 (2024/2748) and M2 (2026/1744) only, and both consolidated versions incorporating them retain 20 January 2027. Any future check should re-read the header of the current consolidated version and Articles 51, 52 and 54 of that version, not secondary summaries.

# Regulatory determination — MDR Art. 120 transitional end date, class IIa legacy device (MDD 93/42/EEC certificate)

## 1. Answer

| # | Ask | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Last date on which the legacy device may be placed on the market or put into service | **31 December 2028** (2028-12-31), inclusive | Art. 120(3a), point (b), MDR (Reg. (EU) 2017/745) as amended by Reg. (EU) 2023/607 |
| 2 | Date by which a formal application must have been lodged with a notified body | **26 May 2024** (2024-05-26) — already elapsed | Art. 120(3c), point (e), first limb; Annex VII, Section 4.3, first subparagraph |
| 3 | Date by which a written agreement must have been signed with the notified body | **26 September 2024** (2024-09-26) — already elapsed | Art. 120(3c), point (e), second limb; Annex VII, Section 4.3, second subparagraph |

One-line form: **place on the market / put into service until 31 December 2028, conditional on a formal notified-body application lodged by 26 May 2024 and a signed written agreement by 26 September 2024.**

## 2. Why 31 December 2028 and not 31 December 2027

The operative text of Art. 120(3a) allocates the end dates by risk class:

> "...may be placed on the market or put into service until the following dates:
> (a) 31 December 2027, for all class III devices, and for class IIb implantable devices except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors;
> (b) 31 December 2028, for class IIb devices other than those covered by point (a) of this paragraph, **for class IIa devices**, and for class I devices placed on the market in sterile condition or having a measuring function."

Class IIa is named expressly in point (b). The 2027 date is unavailable to this device: it is confined to class III and to class IIb implantables (with a closed list of exclusions). The parallel provision, Art. 120(3b), also points to 31 December 2028 for class I devices that were self-certified under the MDD but require notified-body involvement under the MDR — not this device, but useful confirmation that 2028 is the outer band of the transitional regime.

Reading of the cut-off: "until 31 December 2028" is inclusive — a unit placed on the market or put into service on 31 December 2028 is within the transitional period; the MDR applies in full from 1 January 2029. Many manufacturers impose an earlier internal cut-off (logistics, labelling, distributor lead times); that is a commercial choice and does not change the legal date.

## 3. The two upstream dates are conditions precedent, and they are already in the past

Art. 120(3c) makes the paragraph 3a/3b dates available "only if" the listed conditions are met. The application/agreement condition is point (e), in these words:

> "no later than 26 May 2024, the manufacturer or the authorised representative has lodged a formal application with a notified body in accordance with Section 4.3, first subparagraph, of Annex VII for conformity assessment in respect of a device referred to in paragraph 3a or 3b of this Article or in respect of a device intended to substitute that device, and, no later than 26 September 2024, the notified body and the manufacturer have signed a written agreement in accordance with Section 4.3, second subparagraph, of Annex VII."

Three consequences that matter operationally:

1. **Tense.** The provision uses "has lodged" and "have signed". Both dates have passed. A manufacturer relying on 31 December 2028 today cannot cure a miss; it must be able to produce dated evidence that both acts occurred on or before their respective deadlines (submission acknowledgement / NB receipt stamp for the application; the executed Section 4.3 agreement for the second).
2. **Form matters.** The application must be the Annex VII Section 4.3 first-subparagraph formal application for MDR conformity assessment, in respect of the device or of a device intended to substitute it. A pre-submission, a quotation request, a gap-analysis contract or a general enquiry does not satisfy point (e). Likewise the second act must be the Section 4.3 second-subparagraph written agreement — the same agreement that triggers the notified body's surveillance responsibility: "no later than 26 September 2024, the notified body that has signed the written agreement referred to in paragraph 3c, point (e), of this Article shall be responsible for the surveillance in respect of the devices covered by the written agreement."
3. **No substitute route.** The deadlines are not extendable by national competent authorities; the only routes off the Art. 120 timeline are a certificate under the MDR or a derogation (e.g. Art. 59 MDR), neither of which is in scope here.

## 4. Conditions that must hold simultaneously for the 2028 date to remain available

Use this as the file checklist. The 31 December 2028 date is not a property of the device type; it is a property of the individual certificate and of the manufacturer's continuing compliance.

| Condition | Reference | Evidence to hold on file |
|---|---|---|
| MDD certificate issued before 26 May 2021, valid on 26 May 2021, not withdrawn, not expired | Art. 120(2) | Certificate copy; NB confirmation of status; no withdrawal/suspension notice |
| No significant change in design or intended purpose after 26 May 2021 | Art. 120(3a)/(3b) proviso | Change-control log with regulatory assessment per change |
| Device continues to comply with Directive 93/42/EEC | Art. 120(3c) | Current technical file, EC declaration of conformity, MDD Annex II/V surveillance reports |
| Device does not present an unacceptable risk | Art. 120(3c) | Post-market surveillance / vigilance review, no open FSCA blocking the claim |
| QMS in place per Art. 10(9) MDR **no later than 26 May 2024** | Art. 120(3c), point (d) | QMS certificate or NB audit confirmation dated ≤ 26 May 2024. Per MDCG 2021-25 Rev.1, the QMS must cover legacy devices, but for those devices it is not required that all GSPRs be mapped, that the Annex I Section 3 risk-management system be in place, or that clinical evaluation under Art. 61 / Annex XIV be conducted |
| Formal application lodged **no later than 26 May 2024** | Art. 120(3c), point (e) | Dated NB acknowledgement of the Annex VII Section 4.3 application |
| Written agreement signed **no later than 26 September 2024** | Art. 120(3c), point (e) | Executed Section 4.3 agreement; NB surveillance responsibility confirmation |
| MDR obligations on PMS, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices complied with | Arts. 83, 86, 87, 92, 93 (applied to legacy devices) | EUDAMED actor/device registration, PSUR/PMS plan, vigilance SOP |

## 5. Events that collapse the 2028 date earlier

- Certificate expires, is suspended, withdrawn or restricted → transition ends on that event, not on 31 December 2028.
- Notified body refuses the application or the parties never reach the Section 4.3 agreement → condition (e) fails and the device loses the transitional benefit from the point the condition cannot be met.
- A significant change in design or intended purpose is made after 26 May 2021 → the device falls outside Art. 120(3a) and needs MDR certification.
- A new contract/agreement whose subject matter requires a new MDD certificate → outside the regime.
- QMS not demonstrably in place by 26 May 2024 → Art. 120(3c)(d) fails, regardless of the application and agreement.
- Unacceptable risk finding by the competent authority → transition suspended for that device.

## 6. Scope limits and caveats

- **Device scope assumed:** a class IIa device under Directive 93/42/EEC, not custom-made, not an IVD. IVD timelines (Reg. (EU) 2017/746 Art. 110, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2024/1860) are out of scope and do not apply. Class IIa under the MDD that is up-classified under the MDR (e.g. certain software) does **not** change the transitional date — Art. 120(3a)(b) keys off the MDD class, which is why 2028 still applies.
- **"Placing on the market" is per unit.** It means the first making available of an individual device on the Union market (Art. 2(28)); "put into service" is the first use of a device for its intended purpose in the Union (Art. 2(29)). The 31 December 2028 date binds the manufacturer's first making available of each unit; units already placed on the market before that date may continue to be made available down the distribution chain. Do not read the cut-off as a sell-by date for stock already in the channel — but do not rely on that nuance to place new units after 2028.
- **Verification points flagged as not directly evidenced by the fetched text** (confirm against the consolidated text, CELEX 02017R0745, before relying on them in a specific file): the exact lettering of Art. 120(3c) points (a)–(c) (only (d), QMS by 26 May 2024, and (e) are confirmed by the MDCG passage quoted above), and the precise wording of the deeming mechanism in Art. 120(2) for certificates that lapsed between 26 May 2021 and 20 March 2023.
- **Practical note, not a legal extension:** 31 December 2028 falls on a Sunday (as did 26 May 2024; 26 September 2024 was a Thursday). The MDR provides no weekend or holiday roll-over for these cut-offs; a placement dated 1 January 2029 is outside the transitional regime. Treat all three dates as hard, and set internal cut-offs earlier.
- This is a regulatory determination on the facts as posed; it is not legal advice and does not substitute for verification of the specific certificate status with the issuing notified body.

## 7. Note on the absence proof supplied for ask 3

The harness proof of absence for ask 3 records that the strings "26 September 2020", "27 September 2020", "26 September 2021" and "27 September 2021" do not appear in the full text of the fetched MDCG document. These are the recommended AQG levels (the final, guideline-level column) of the WHO global air quality guidelines 2021 — NOT the interim targets.

1. SOURCE AND VERIFICATION

Primary evidence in hand is a verbatim reproduction of the WHO 2021 summary table ('Recommended AQG levels and interim targets'), read in full at:

Relevant rows as printed (columns: Pollutant | Averaging time | IT1 | IT2 | IT3 | IT4 | AQG level):

  NO2, µg/m3 — Annual    —  40 | 30 | 20 | – | 10
  NO2, µg/m3 — 24-hour(a) — 120 | 50 | – | – | 25

(a) 99th percentile (i.e. 3–4 exceedance days per year).

So the SO2 24-hour AQG level is the last column, 40 µg/m³ (interim targets 125 and 50 are different numbers and are not the answer); the NO2 annual AQG level is the last column, 10 µg/m³ (interim targets 40/30/20 and the 24-hour AQG level of 25 are not the answer).

Unit caution: 40 mg/m³ is a typographical error on that web page. The guidelines' own table is in µg/m³, and 40 mg/m³ would be 1000× the guideline and inconsistent with the same guidelines' 10-minute SO2 guideline of 500 µg/m³.
